# Present2u

> Present2u turns a deck into source code. Write a P2U/1 manifest — maths,
> diagrams, code and layouts — and compile it to a live presenter, a
> self-contained HTML file, a PDF, or speaker notes. Agents can drive the whole
> thing over the CLI, a JSON API, or an MCP server.

Present2u is a Rails app (built on Writebook) with a declarative presentation
compiler, **P2U/1**, on top. Manifests compile to slides; diagrams (D2), equations
(LaTeX) and Typst documents render server-side to SVG; code is highlighted with
Rouge; inline maths renders in the browser with KaTeX.

## Quick start

```console
$ git clone https://github.com/Oreoro/present2u && cd present2u/writebook
```

```console
$ bin/setup                      # install deps, prepare db
$ bin/rails server -p 3010       # app at http://localhost:3010

$ bin/p2u validate talk.p2u
$ bin/p2u compile  talk.p2u --render --json
$ bin/p2u export   talk.p2u --to html   # single-file deck (diagrams inlined)
$ bin/p2u export   talk.p2u --to notes  # speaker notes
$ bin/p2u mcp                           # MCP server on stdio
```

## The P2U/1 manifest

A manifest is YAML, JSON, or Markdown with front-matter. Minimal shape:

```yaml
p2u: 1
deck:
  title: Attention Is All You Need
  subtitle: The Transformer, end to end
  author: Present2u
  theme: white        # writebook | white | black | blue | green | magenta | orange | violet
  scroll: false       # true = a flowing page instead of 16:9 frames
slides:
  - layout: section
    title: Attention
    body: The Transformer, end to end
  - layout: content
    title: Why divide by sqrt(d_k)?
    body: |
      Scaling keeps the softmax in a useful range: $ \sqrt{d_k} $.
  - layout: equation
    blocks:
      - kind: equation
        source: \mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V
```

### Layouts

`title`, `section`, `content`, `two-column`, `compare`, `code-split`,
`full-code`, `diagram`, `equation`, `table`, `metric-row`, `timeline`, `quote`,
`image`, `image-grid`, `references`, `recap`, `qa`, `end`, `divider`
(legacy aliases: `page`, `picture`, `typst`).

### Blocks (used by multi-block layouts)

| kind | fields |
| --- | --- |
| `markdown` | `body` (Markdown) |
| `code` | `body`, `lang` |
| `diagram` | `lang` (`d2`, `d2-sketch`, `tala`), `source` |
| `equation` | `source` (LaTeX) |
| `table` | `head`, `rows` |
| `metric` | `label`, `value`, `detail` |
| `quote` | `text`, `cite` |
| `callout` | `body`, `tone` |
| `image` | `url`, `caption` |
| `definition` | `term`, `description` |
| `references` | `items` |
| `notes-only`, `spacer` | — |

Every slide accepts `notes:` (speaker notes, Markdown). Get the full field
reference with `bin/p2u schema` (or the `p2u_get_schema` MCP tool).

### Worked examples

`examples/` ships complete manifests — `raft.p2u` (technical), and
`urbanevents-pitch.p2u` (a business pitch using `metric-row`, `timeline`,
`diagram` and fee math).

Diagram/code/equation fences also work inside `markdown` bodies:

- ` ```d2 ` — D2 diagram, TALA layout
- ` ```d2-sketch ` — hand-drawn D2
- ` ```latex ` — arbitrary LaTeX → SVG
- ` ```typst ` — Typst document → SVG
- ` $...$ ` / ` $$...$$ ` — inline KaTeX maths

### Stability and idempotency

Give slides an `id` to get stable plan/apply diffs:

```yaml
slides:
  - id: intro
    layout: section
    title: Introduction
```

`plan` diffs a manifest against a deck; `apply` creates/updates/deletes/reorders
by `id` (with positional fallback) and is idempotent.

## CLI

```
bin/p2u validate <file>            [--json]
bin/p2u compile  <file> [--render] [--json]
bin/p2u outline  <file>            [--json]
bin/p2u plan     <file> --deck ID
bin/p2u apply    <file> --deck ID --user EMAIL
bin/p2u export   <file> --to html|notes|pdf [--out PATH]
bin/p2u compose  "<prompt>"        [--slides N] [--theme NAME]
bin/p2u mcp
bin/p2u schema
bin/p2u doctor
```

## JSON API

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <user.api_token>`.

```
GET  /api/decks
POST /api/decks/import              # body: P2U manifest
POST /api/compile                   # validate + plan
POST /api/compose                   # prompt -> manifest
POST /api/export                    # -> { content }
GET  /api/schema
GET  /api/toolchain
POST /api/decks/:id/plan
POST /api/decks/:id/apply
```

## MCP

`bin/p2u mcp` (or `bin/p2u-mcp`, which finds a modern Ruby) speaks MCP over
stdio. Tools: `p2u_guide`, `p2u_get_schema`, `p2u_validate`, `p2u_compile`,
`p2u_outline`, `p2u_compose`, `p2u_render`, `p2u_export`, `p2u_list_templates`,
`p2u_list_decks`, `p2u_get_deck`, `p2u_create_deck`, `p2u_compose_deck`,
`p2u_plan`, `p2u_apply`, `p2u_doctor`. Resources: `p2u://guide`, `p2u://skill`,
`p2u://schema`.

## Design system

One light theme everywhere — chrome, decks and slides share tokens:

- Ink `#37352F`, page `#FFFFFF`, subtle surface `#F7F7F5`, hairline `#E9E9E7`,
  secondary text `#787774`, accent `#2383E2` (Notion-flavoured).
- D2 renders in ink (`#37352f`) on a `#f7f7f5` fill; Typst and LaTeX render in
  `currentColor`; code uses Rouge with a Notion-flavoured palette.
- Typography is the system UI stack; headings weight 600.

## Toolchain

`d2` (TALA), `typst`, `pdflatex` + `pdftocairo`, Ruby 3.4, Node. Run
`bin/p2u doctor` to check.

## Rules for agents

1. Call `p2u_guide` (or read this file) before authoring.
2. Always `validate`/`compile` and fix diagnostics before creating a deck.
3. Check `outline` density: keep a slide under ~45 words and one idea.
4. Prefer `id` on slides so `plan`/`apply` are stable and idempotent.
5. Never commit secrets; the app reads `P2U_LLM_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
